newsitem.title: INDIA: Highlights of India-Bangladesh Ganges water treaty.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of India-Bangladesh Ganges water treaty.

text.p: Following are the highlights of a treaty signed on Thursday by India and Bangladesh to share the waters of the Ganges River, which flows into Bangladesh from eastern India:
--The formula to share water under the treaty will be decided by the flow of water at the Farakka Barrage near the India-Bangladesh border.
--Whenever the flow of water is less than 70,000 cusecs (cubic feet per second) at Farakka, both countries will share the flow evenly.

--In the lean season between March 1 and May 10 every year, when the water flow usually falls below 70,000 cusecs, each country will receive a guaranteed flow of 35,000 cusecs in an alternating sequence of 10-day periods.
--When the flow is between 70,000 and 75,000 cusecs, Bangladesh will receive 35,000 cusecs and India the balance.
--When the flow is more than 75,000 cusecs, India will receive 40,000 cusecs and Bangladesh the balance.
--The 30-year treaty will be reviewed mandatorily every five years. It would be open to either country to seed the first review after two years to assess the impact and working of the treaty.

--During the period of the treaty, in the absence of a mutual agreement on adjustments during reviews, India will release water downstream at Farakka no less than 90 percent of Bangladesh's share according to the water-sharing formula.

--If the flow at Farakka falls below 50,000 cusecs in any 10-day period, both countries will enter into immediate consultations for an emergency solution based on equity and fair play with no harm to either country.
